checklist.detail: Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy: computed wall temp 1334 K EXCEEDS its 1250 K max service temp (Tc 3618 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~11.3 kW/m2K incl. carbon-deposit credit, T_aw ~3623 K, coolant ~37 m/s (coolant-side wall ~991 K), 0.20 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.1, regen): wall ~1351 K, 0.93x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: At the throat, combined hoop + thermal-restraint stress (Huzel eq 4-27/4-28, tube_wall) is ~678 MPa (hoop ~40 MPa from a ~3.2 MPa net jacket-vs-gas differential + thermal-restraint ~638 MPa) against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5), with the wall at its minimum-stress thickness ~0.20 mm. This uses a real handbook stress formula (Huzel eq 4-27/4-28, tube_wall), not a proxy - worth a closer structural look. The thermal-restraint term dominates and grows with wall thickness (dT = q*t/k), so the wall is already at its ~0.2 mm minimum - consider a higher-conductivity liner (a copper alloy such as GRCop-84/NARloy-Z) or less throat heat flux (film cooling, lower Pc).
